strategies.name: Naive Sequential All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Exactly mirrors the reference: 8 sequential all_reduce calls with interleaved local bidiagonal coupling/decoupling operations. 8 collective dispatches total. Represents the baseline with maximum readability but no fusion or overlapping of communication and computation.

strategies.name: Fused Local-Op Batching Between Collectives
strategies.desc: Group multiple coupling/decoupling loops into single vectorized operations or combine division-by-W with coupling in one pass to reduce memory passes. Still 8 all_reduce dispatches but reduces local compute overhead through better cache locality and fewer temporary buffer allocations.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Replace each all_reduce with reduce_scatter followed by all_gather, enabling local work (coupling/decoupling) to happen on smaller per-rank shards between the two phases. 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but each operates on W×smaller payload (size S instead of W×S), potentially better network utilization on hierarchical topologies.

strategies.name: Pipelined Overlapped Communication-Computation
strategies.desc: Split the W×S vector into chunks and pipeline all_reduce on chunk[i] while performing local coupling operations on chunk[i-1]. Uses async collectives or manual chunking with multiple dispatch streams. Higher dispatch count (8×chunks) but overlaps communication latency with computation, critical for large W=224.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction Tree
strategies.desc:
Exploit multi-node structure by performing intra-node all_reduce (across cores_per_device × num_devices within each node) followed by inter-node all_reduce, applied at each of the 8 stages. 16 collective dispatches (8 intra + 8 inter) but leverages faster shared-memory or NVLink within nodes to reduce cross-node traffic and latency.
